origin.description: Exponentially tilted multinomial weights so a linear approximation has a chosen mean.
origin.usage: exp.tilt(L, theta = NULL, t0 = 0, lambda = NULL, strata = rep(1, length(L)))

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values, one per observation. The same length as the original sample.

arguments.name: theta
arguments.text: Mean required for the linear approximation. Needed when lambda is omitted.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Observed value of the statistic. Subtracted before the multiplier is solved, then added back. The default is 0.

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.text: Lagrange multiplier. Probabilities are proportional to exp(lambda * L) within each stratum. If theta is also supplied, lambda is ignored and recomputed.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Stratum labels, one per observation. The default is a single sample.

origin.details: Within each stratum the weights are proportional to exp(lambda * L / n). lambda is chosen by BFGS so the tilted mean of the influence values equals theta - t0. The search stops when the squared error is at most 1e-6; a larger error is an error. One theta gives a probability vector. Several thetas give a matrix with one row per target. A supplied vector of multipliers and no theta returns a single theta: t0 plus the sum of the probabilities times L, recycled in column-major order.
origin.value: A list with p (the tilted probabilities), theta, and lambda.

translation.description: Exponentially tilted multinomial weights so a linear approximation has a chosen mean.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values, one per observation.

arguments.name: theta
arguments.text: Mean required for the linear approximation. Needed when lambda_ is omitted.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Observed value of the statistic. Subtracted before the multiplier is solved, then added back. The default is 0.

arguments.name: lambda_
arguments.text: Lagrange multiplier. The name is lambda_ because lambda is reserved. Probabilities are proportional to exp(lambda_ * L) within each stratum. If theta is also supplied, lambda_ is ignored and recomputed.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Stratum labels, one per observation. None puts every observation in one sample.

translation.details: Within each stratum the weights are proportional to exp(lambda_ * L / n). The multiplier is the same one-dimensional BFGS search as optim: central differences with step 1e-3, and the inverse Hessian resets to 1 after two accepted steps. The search stops when the squared error of the tilted mean is at most 1e-6. One theta returns p as a vector. Several thetas return a matrix with one row per target. A supplied vector of multipliers and no theta returns one theta: t0 plus the sum of the probabilities times L, recycled in column-major order.
translation.value: An ExpTilt with p, theta, and lambda_. Printing it shows all three.
translation.example:
from boot.tilt import exp_tilt

L = [-1.2, 0.3, 0.5, -0.4, 1.1, 0.2, -0.7, 0.8]
print(exp_tilt(L, theta=[0.4, -0.2], t0=0.1))
